mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which may lead to decreased borrowing and spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of cases when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 5% indicates a weakening labor market, which may lead to decreased consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of cases when UNRATE exceeds 5%, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) reflects strong demand in the housing market, which may boost related industries and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the Rank IC for HOUST and S&P 500 returns is below 0.03, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) growth may signal supply chain issues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of cases when INDPRO growth is negative, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When both employment (PAYEMS) increases and unemployment (UNRATE) rises, it may indicate inefficiencies in the labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of cases when PAYEMS and UNRATE move inversely, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) combined with low retail sales (RSAFS) may indicate stagflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the Rank IC for the interaction of FEDFUNDS and RSAFS is below 0.03, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, rising CPI (CPIAUCSL) may lead to tighter monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of cases when CPIAUCSL rises in late-cycle, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates a strong economy, which may boost corporate earnings and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the Rank IC for GDPC1 and S&P 500 returns is below 0.03, the hypothesis is rejected.
